operations.summary: Bulk-upload products to one or more stores from supplier products, a file, or finder categories.
operations.notes: Bulk-upload products to one or more stores. Async: starts an asynchronous bulk job and returns immediately with {"status": "Product uploading started", "bulk_action": {...}}; poll progress by passing bulk_action.id to get_bulk_action_items (autods-bulk-actions manifest). Provide at least ONE product source in the body: new_products, file_url, or finder_categories. The asin in new_products is the supplier's product id, usually embedded in the product URL (e.g. Amazon B0D8HR6M4B from .../dp/B0D8HR6M4B/...) — pass the bare id or the full product URL, not a search/category landing page. If status=5 (scheduled), upload_settings.scheduled_datetime is required and must be a future, timezone-aware time. region, status and buy_site_id are integer enums whose values are listed on each field.

parameters.name: store_ids
parameters.description: AutoDS store IDs if more than one should be comma separated

body_schema.description: Provide at least one product source: new_products, file_url, or finder_categories.

region.description: Region the products are uploaded for, as an INTEGER enum value: 1=us, 2=uk, 3=de, 4=fr, 5=it, 6=cn, 7=all_regions, 8=th, 9=es, 10=au, 11=ca, 12=pl, 13=ru, 14=be, 15=cz, 16=vn, 17=my, 18=sg, 19=ph, 20=id, 21=br, 22=ie.

buy_site_id.description: Supplier (source) site the products come from, as an INTEGER enum value: 1=amazon, 2=aliexpress, 3=banggood, 4=walmart, 5=homedepot, 6=wayfair, 7=costco, 8=overstock, 9=costway, 10=chinabrands, 11=etsy, 12=lowes, 13=ebay, 14=target, 15=cjdropshipping, 16=samsclub, 17=vidaxl, 18=gearbest, 19=miniinthebox, 20=lightinthebox, 21=alibaba, 22=pureformulas, 23=redbubble, 24=wish, 25=kmart, 26=dhgate, 27=autods_marketplace, 28=shein, 29=macys, 30=kohls, 31=catch, 32=shopify, 33=autods_sourcing, 34=temu, 35=cdiscount, 36=print_on_demand, 37=tiktok, 38=alibaba_1688, 39=kogan.

asin.description: Supplier product id or full product URL (required).

file_url.description: URL of a file/CSV of products to import.

scheduled_datetime.description: ISO 8601 datetime; required when status=5 (scheduled), must be future & timezone-aware.

parameters.name: store_ids
parameters.description: AutoDS store IDs if more than one should be comma separated

operations.notes: Imports draft products to the marketplace (the selling channel — eBay, Shopify, etc.) in bulk. Async: starts an asynchronous import job and returns immediately with {"status": ..., "bulk_action": {...}}; poll bulk_action.id via get_bulk_action_items (autods-bulk-actions manifest). product_status selects which products to act on. OMIT `filters` to import ALL products of that status (rarely intended); to target specific products filter by id ({"name": "id", "op": "in", "value_type": "list", "value_list": [...]}, or op "=" with value_type "object_id" for one).

product_status.description: Selects which products to act on: 1=draft, 2=active, 3=ended, 4=untracked, 5=scheduled, 6=pre_draft.

filters.description: Selects which products to import. Omit to import ALL products of that status.

name.description: Filterable field name. Filter by `id` with value_type `object_id` (24-character hex string).

value.description: Single-value operand. Enum-valued fields take their INTEGER value, not the name.

value_list.description: Multi-value operand; REQUIRED for in/not_in and for value_type list/list_int.

parameters.name: store_ids
parameters.description: AutoDS store IDs if more than one should be comma separated

operations.notes:
Read-only POST. Queries products by filter and returns {results: [...]}. Filterable fields include title, tags, note, status, site_id, variations.price, variations.quantity, variations.inventory_status, variations.active_buy_item.price/site_id/region, error_list.error_type, created_date, upload_date, total_sold_count, views, watchers, etc. There is no top-level `region` field — the item's region is `variations.active_buy_item.region`. Enum-valued filter values take their INTEGER value, never the name — every allowed value is listed on the `filters[].value` schema of this tool. Filter by `id` with value_type `object_id` (each id is a 24-character hex string); multi-value ops (in/not_in) and value_type list/list_int put their values in `value_list`. Product objects are LARGE (variations, images, description, item_specifics): for listing/summary use cases ALWAYS pass `projection` (e.g. ["title","main_picture_url","variations.price","amount_of_variations","total_sold_count","item_id_on_site","upload_date"]) and/or a small `limit` — a full-object page of 100 can exceed ~80 KB and overflow response token limits. Keep `main_picture_url` in any projection you send: it is what the thumbnail grid is built from, and a projection without it returns a grid of empty cells rather than no grid at all.

Product images: the first 20 results' image URLs also arrive in an `images` block beside `data`, rewritten to a ~256px thumbnail where the sell channel's CDN offers one — about half of them do, and the rest render at full size in a small cell, which costs bandwidth rather than tokens. A client that renders MCP Apps shows them as a thumbnail grid; Claude Code, Cursor and MCP Inspector render no widget and show the URLs instead. The block is built from whatever the response actually carries, so a `projection` that omits `main_picture_url` (and `images`) yields an `images` block whose every entry has no URL — the client still draws the grid, and every cell reads "no image". That is the one way to make this tool look broken while it answers 200, so project `main_picture_url` whenever a person will see the result. There is deliberately no `include_images` base64 option on this tool: roughly half of these images have no small variant to fetch, so the model would be sent full-size originals to downscale.

When `product_status` is 2 (active) or 1 (draft), each entry in that block also carries a `link` to that product's own page in the AutoDS web app — a client that renders the grid makes the thumbnail clickable, and the URL is in the block either way, so it can be offered to the user as a plain link. Products of any other status carry no link: the app has no page that lists one product of theirs, and a link to a page without the product on it is worse than none.

product_status.description: Required INTEGER enum value (NOT the name — sending a string like "active" returns HTTP 422): 1=draft, 2=active, 3=ended, 4=untracked, 5=scheduled, 6=pre_draft.

name.description: Filterable field name. Filter by `id` with value_type `object_id` (24-character hex string).

value.description: Single-value operand. Enum-valued fields take their INTEGER value, never the name; every set is listed here, so building a filter needs no other tool. `status` 1=draft, 2=active, 3=ended, 4=untracked, 5=scheduled, 6=pre_draft. `variations.inventory_status` 1=in_stock, 2=out_of_stock, 3=on_hold. `error_list.error_type` 0=vero_error, 1=internal_error, 2=untracked_error, 3=monitor_error, 4=upload_error, 5=supplier_changes_error, 6=draft_error_reason, 7=file_exchange, 8=facebook_helper, 9=selling_channel_changes. `variations.active_buy_item.region` 1=us, 2=uk, 3=de, 4=fr, 5=it, 6=cn, 7=all_regions, 8=th, 9=es, 10=au, 11=ca, 12=pl, 13=ru, 14=be, 15=cz, 16=vn, 17=my, 18=sg, 19=ph, 20=id, 21=br, 22=ie. The two site fields are DIFFERENT enums — do not mix them: `site_id` is the selling channel (1=ebay, 2=amazon, 3=shopify, 4=facebook, 5=wix, 6=woocommerce, 7=etsy, 8=tiktok), while `variations.active_buy_item.site_id` is the supplier the item is sourced from (1=amazon, 2=aliexpress, 3=banggood, 4=walmart, 5=homedepot, 6=wayfair, 7=costco, 8=overstock, 9=costway, 10=chinabrands, 11=etsy, 12=lowes, 13=ebay, 14=target, 15=cjdropshipping, 16=samsclub, 17=vidaxl, 18=gearbest, 19=miniinthebox, 20=lightinthebox, 21=alibaba, 22=pureformulas, 23=redbubble, 24=wish, 25=kmart, 26=dhgate, 27=autods_marketplace, 28=shein, 29=macys, 30=kohls, 31=catch, 32=shopify, 33=autods_sourcing, 34=temu, 35=cdiscount, 36=print_on_demand, 37=tiktok, 38=alibaba_1688, 39=kogan).

value_list.description: Multi-value operand; REQUIRED for in/not_in and for value_type list/list_int.

operations.summary: Delete one product from a store, and optionally its live listing on the sell channel.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: ONE AutoDS store id. This tool takes a single store, not the comma-separated `store_ids` the other product tools take.

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: The AutoDS product id: the 24-character hex `id` that list_products returns, not the marketplace item id.

parameters.name: remove_from_marketplace
parameters.description: Required, and there is no default — decide it for this product and say which you chose. true also deletes the listing from the user's sell channel (Shopify, eBay, …), so buyers stop seeing it; this is what cleaning up an unwanted live listing means. false removes the product from AutoDS only and leaves the listing live on the channel, with nothing monitoring its price or stock any more. For a product that never reached the channel (a draft, a scheduled product) the flag changes nothing.

operations.notes:
Deletes ONE product from ONE store. It starts no bulk job, so there is nothing to poll. The response is {"status": "Product <marketplace item id> was deleted successfully"}. One exception to read the answer by: on an eBay MIP store, called with remove_from_marketplace true, the product's own status change is finished off in the background, so it can still come back in list_products for a few seconds after the 200 — re-read the store rather than reading the delay as a failed delete.

Irreversible. The product stops being tracked, leaves the list_products results for its old status, and nothing in this server puts it back — re-listing it means uploading it again with upload_products and redoing whatever pricing and settings it carried. With remove_from_marketplace true the buyer-facing listing is deleted from the sell channel as well, which is the half the user cannot undo themselves.

An agent must not call this unless the user asked, in that turn, for this particular product to be removed. It needs the Drafts or EndProducts privilege group; without it the call answers `forbidden`, and get_user_subscription is what shows the caller's add-ons.

Retrying after a failed or timed-out call is safe. A delete that already landed answers `upstream_client_error` the second time — the product is gone, or is already ended — rather than removing anything else. To establish whether the first call landed, read the store with list_products.

operations.summary: Re-link one product's variations to the supplier offer attached to its sourcing request.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: ONE AutoDS store id — the store the product is in. Not the comma-separated `store_ids` the list tools take.

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: The AutoDS product id: the 24-character hex `id` list_products returns.

operations.notes:
Points one product's variations at the supplier offer attached to its sourcing request, which makes that offer the product's supplier. It spends no credit and can be called again with different pairings.

It is NOT needed after create_1688_sourcing_request — that one call creates the request and links the variations together. This tool is for re-linking afterwards: correcting which product variation maps to which supplier variation, or picking the pairings up again after the request was switched to a different quoted offer in the AutoDS web app.

The request must already have a supplier offer — status `ready` or `linked`. On `new` or `in_progress` the call is refused as `upstream_client_error` saying the request is in the wrong status; that is the documented answer, not a fault, so read the status with list_store_quotes first. A request on another store answers not-found. The account needs an active Order Processing add-on; without it the call answers `upstream_client_error`, which here means the add-on rather than a bad request.

`store_quote_id` is the sourcing request's own integer id: the `id` of a list_store_quotes result. In `variations_match`, `item_id_on_site` is the SUPPLIER variation id — the offer id, an underscore, then the supplier's own variation id, e.g. "992906129243_6280495563187" — while `sku` and `variant_id_on_site` identify the AutoDS side of the pair. One of the two is required on every entry once the list has more than one entry. A single entry may omit both, but only on a product with one variation: on a product with several, an entry that names neither links nothing, and nothing reports it. A variation left out of the list keeps whatever supplier it had, so the product ends up sourced from two places at once, half of it automated and half of it not.

The answer is the product as it now stands, with its new supplier item; `ok` is transport-level only. `add_to_unfulfilled_orders: true` also re-points the product's orders that are still waiting to be fulfilled at the new supplier, and that part is finished off in the background, so it is not done when this call returns.

store_quote_id.description: The sourcing request's own integer id: the `id` of a list_store_quotes result.

add_to_unfulfilled_orders.description: Required, and there is no default — decide it for this product and say which you chose. true also re-points the product's orders that are still waiting to be fulfilled at the new supplier. false leaves those orders pointing where they already point. For a product with no unfulfilled orders the flag changes nothing.

variations_match.description: One entry per product variation being linked. A variation with no entry keeps its old supplier.

item_id_on_site.description: The SUPPLIER variation id: the offer id, an underscore, then the supplier's own variation id, e.g. "992906129243_6280495563187".

sku.description: The AutoDS variation's SKU. Either this or `variant_id_on_site` identifies the AutoDS side of the pair.

variant_id_on_site.description: The AutoDS variation's id on the sell channel. The alternative to `sku`.
